method: One evaluator (agent resolve-edge-model-test) read the new fact and every disputed fact of each case and applied the rules of the resolve_edge prompt: duplicate = identical factual information; contradiction = the new fact updates, supersedes, or is incompatible with the fact. A newer measurement, version, state, or count of the same thing counts as an update. Verdicts: baseline = base1 is right, candidate = the candidate is right, unclear = both answers are defensible. Reasons are abstract because the facts come from the private graph.

judgments.reason: Two facts mention the old CPU limit only as a qualifier of a workload description. The baseline invalidates them, the candidate does not.
The extra idx of base1 is about a server, not about the changed route. base2 agrees with the candidate.
Same document version with a different commit id: an update. base2 agrees with the candidate.
Two older facts say that a page does not exist; the new fact says that it exists. base1 misses them, base2 and the candidate invalidate them.
The count of stranded drafts changed from three to four. The candidate keeps the old counts current.
A newer build of the same site with new page counts. The baseline invalidates all older build snapshots; the candidate keeps 4 of 10 current without a clear rule.
Newer search metrics for one page. The candidate keeps two older snapshots current.
A new public release replaces the old one. The candidate keeps the fact that the public pointer targets the old release.
Newer 28-day analytics. base1 misses two older snapshots; base2 and the candidate invalidate them.
Different credentials live in different stores. They do not contradict each other.
The new fact says that one item was released; the old fact says that this item is still a gap. The candidate misses it.
New test file layout versus one older single-file suite. The new layout can replace or add to the old one.
The new fact says that a meaning page exists; the old fact says that only a glossary entry exists. The candidate misses it.
The old fact names one single reason why payments are closed; the new fact adds a second gate.
The new fact reports a successful render; the old fact says that the new render failed. The candidate misses it.
The new fact is a subset of the related fact, not identical information. base1 marks a duplicate; base2 and the candidate do not.
base1 invalidates a fact about a different product. base2 and the candidate do not.
The new fact is a subset of a related fact. base1 and base2 merge it; the candidate keeps it as a new edge. No information is lost in either case.
The new fact says that ad code exists and can be switched off; three old facts say that no ad code exists yet. luna-low misses all three.
A new deployed image digest. luna-low keeps three older image pins current.
Redirect rules replace an older alias setup. luna-low misses both old facts.
luna-low marks two consistent facts as contradicted: one says the same thing, the other is about a different branch.
